summary:
Silent Travelers is an interactive, bilingual WebGL museum that brings NASA’s retired and abandoned spacecraft back into the spotlight. Visitors travel through a dark chronological tunnel containing 13 stories, arranged from the present toward the past. As they move forward, each artifact and the next exhibit illuminate, transforming exploration into a trail of light.

Visitors can examine mission-specific 3D models, view verified archival imagery, read story-driven explanations, and launch simulated journeys from Earth to the locations where the spacecraft remain. These journeys include synchronized narration and subtitles, Martian dust storms, seismic events, lunar rover tracks, and representative planetary terrain.

The project makes complex mission history approachable for school-age and casual space enthusiasts without sacrificing scientific traceability. It concludes with a Space Travelers Certificate and invites visitors to consider whether off-world hardware should be understood as space debris or as humanity’s scientific and cultural heritage.
details:
Silent Travelers is a browser-based, interactive 3D museum designed around NASA’s “Discarded Equipment Storytelling” challenge. It focuses on 13 representative artifacts connected to the Moon, Mars, asteroids, and deep space: Apollo Lunar Modules, Lunar Roving Vehicles, ALSEP packages, Surveyor landers, Sojourner, Opportunity, Viking, InSight, Dawn, NEAR Shoemaker, Pioneer 10 and 11, Ingenuity, and the Kepler Space Telescope.

The museum is presented as a dark, horseshoe-shaped chronological tunnel. Visitors move smoothly along its center line using the mouse wheel and look freely with the mouse. The artifacts are ordered from the present toward the past. The first exhibit is illuminated at the entrance, and approaching it activates the next exhibit. Lights behind the visitor remain on, while unexplored sections stay dark. This creates a visual timeline in which every newly discovered story leaves a permanent trail of light.

When visitors approach an exhibit and look directly at it, a separate archival record appears. The exhibit backdrop and the close-up archival record use different images wherever suitable material is available. Each story explains how the spacecraft was constructed, what scientific contribution it made, and why it stopped operating or remained in space.

Visitors can also select “Travel to where I was left” to launch an educational journey from Earth to the artifact’s destination. Opportunity’s simulation includes a planet-wide Martian dust storm and accumulating dust. InSight’s experience includes a marsquake followed by windblown surface dust. Lunar wheeled vehicles leave appropriately scaled tracks. Recorded narration is accompanied by synchronized English or Turkish subtitles. Local terrain, flight duration, and planetary distances are clearly identified as educational simulations rather than exact real-time ephemeris calculations.

The project includes English and Turkish language modes, an introductory visitor brochure, progress tracking, a Space Travelers Certificate, a museum feedback wall, and a final question asking whether abandoned space hardware represents scientific heritage or space debris.

The application was developed using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Three.js, WebGL, GLB 3D models, browser audio, and responsive interface techniques. NASA mission archives, coordinates, imagery, reports, and 3D resources were used for scientific traceability. When an official NASA model was unavailable, the interface explicitly labels the model as user-provided or as an educational reconstruction.

The intended impact is to help young visitors form an emotional connection with robotic explorers while learning how engineering made scientific discovery possible. Instead of presenting missions as isolated lists of facts, Silent Travelers allows visitors to walk through their history, hear their stories, and confront the question of how humanity should preserve its off-world heritage.
